answer: Verifiable delay minting resists sybils: each identity's key must pass through a sequential function that cannot be parallelized — ivory-hard wall-clock time at the forge, not raw core count. A farm with a thousand machines cannot ripple a thousand keys out faster than one, because the work is inherently serial per identity. Honest agents wait once; a swarm must serve the same irreducible delay for every head, so mass minting cannot be sped up by buying more hardware.
